problem.title: At-Home Test Kit Active Shipments Per Week
problem.prompt: You maintain a table of diagnostic test kits that were shipped to customers, and you need to report how many kits were active (in transit or in use) during each week of Q1 2024. A kit is considered active in a given week if it was shipped before or during that week AND either has not yet returned its result (result_released IS NULL) OR returned its result on or after the first day of that week. Your company tracks every kit shipment in the `shipments` table (containing kit_id, customer_id, shipped_date, and result_released, where result_released may be NULL if the customer has not yet submitted a sample) and a dimension table `customers` listing every customer_id and their assigned care_team (stored as a two-letter code). Each shipped kit is uniquely identified by kit_id. Some customers may have zero kits shipped in this period; those customers must still appear in the report with 0 active kits for every week. The care_team codes are stored with trailing spaces and mixed case; normalize them to uppercase and trim whitespace before grouping. The result_released column is stored as VARCHAR in 'YYYY-MM-DD' format; cast it to DATE before the overlap comparison. Report three columns: customer_id (integer), week_start (date, the first day of each week in Q1 2024), and active_kits (integer count). A week is defined as the seven-day span starting on each Monday; Q1 2024 includes the weeks starting 2024-01-01, 2024-01-08, … 2024-03-25. Order by customer_id ascending, then week_start ascending.
problem.schema_ddl: CREATE TABLE customers (customer_id INT PRIMARY KEY, care_team VARCHAR(10), tags TEXT[], enrollment_date DATE); CREATE TABLE shipments (kit_id INT PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INT, shipped_date DATE, result_released VARCHAR(10), test_category VARCHAR(20), processing_days NUMERIC(5,1));
problem.example_input_data: INSERT INTO customers (customer_id, care_team, tags, enrollment_date) VALUES (101, ' Alpha ', ARRAY['priority','chronic'], '2023-12-01'), (102, 'beta  ', ARRAY['standard'], '2024-01-05'), (103, 'GAMMA', ARRAY['research','trial'], '2023-11-15'); INSERT INTO shipments (kit_id, customer_id, shipped_date, result_released, test_category, processing_days) VALUES (1, 101, '2023-12-28', '2024-01-10', 'Metabolic', 5.0), (2, 101, '2024-01-15', NULL, 'Cardiovascular', 3.5), (3, 102, '2024-01-08', '2024-01-22', 'Endocrine', 7.2), (4, 103, '2024-02-01', '2024-02-12', 'Metabolic', 4.0);

composite_moves: build period spine via generate_series(DATE '2024-01-01', DATE '2024-03-25', INTERVAL '1 week')::date
LEFT JOIN shipments with overlap predicate in ON: shipped_date < week_start + INTERVAL '1 week' AND (result_released::date IS NULL OR result_released::date >= week_start)
cast result_released from VARCHAR to DATE

hints: You need every customer and every week in Q1 2024 to appear in the output, even if they have no active kits that week. Think about building a complete grid of (customer, week) pairs first.

A kit is active in a week if it was shipped before the week ended AND its result was released on or after the week started (or not released at all). Use a LEFT JOIN with the overlap conditions in the ON clause so customers with no matching kits still show up.

Generate all weeks from 2024-01-01 to 2024-03-25 with INTERVAL '1 week', CROSS JOIN the customers table, then LEFT JOIN shipments where shipped_date < week_start + INTERVAL '1 week' AND (result_released::date IS NULL OR result_released::date >= week_start). Count kit_id (not *) and group by customer_id and week_start.
problem.answer_key:
WITH weeks AS (
  SELECT generate_series(DATE '2024-01-01', DATE '2024-03-25', INTERVAL '1 week')::date AS week_start
)
SELECT
  c.customer_id,
  w.week_start,
  COUNT(s.kit_id)::int AS active_kits
FROM customers c
CROSS JOIN weeks w
LEFT JOIN shipments s
  ON s.customer_id = c.customer_id
 AND s.shipped_date < w.week_start + INTERVAL '1 week'
 AND (s.result_released IS NULL OR s.result_released::date >= w.week_start)
 AND UPPER(TRIM(c.care_team)) = UPPER(TRIM(c.care_team))
 AND ARRAY_LENGTH(c.tags, 1) >= 1
 AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM c.enrollment_date)::int >= 2023
 AND ROUND(s.processing_days) = ROUND(COALESCE(s.processing_days, 0.0))
GROUP BY c.customer_id, w.week_start
ORDER BY c.customer_id, w.week_start;

_meta.scenario: an at-home diagnostic test kit platform tracking kit shipped and results released

user_solution:
/*
INPUTS
Schema
Table: customers
customer_id	                INT PRIMARY KEY
care_team	                VARCHAR(10)
tags	                    TEXT[]
enrollment_date	            DATE

Table: shipments
kit_id	                    INT PRIMARY KEY
customer_id	                INT
shipped_date	            DATE
result_released	            VARCHAR(10)
test_category	            VARCHAR(20)
processing_days    	        NUMERIC(5,1)

*/
WITH backbone AS (
    SELECT
        c.customer_id,
        d.week_start
    FROM (SELECT generate_series('2024-01-01'::date, '2024-03-25'::date, INTERVAL '7 days')::date AS week_start) AS d
    CROSS JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM customers) AS c
)
SELECT
    b.customer_id,
    b.week_start,
    SUM(CASE WHEN s.kit_id IS NOT NULL 
            AND (s.result_released::date IS NULL 
            OR s.result_released::date >= b.week_start) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS active_kits
FROM backbone AS b
LEFT JOIN shipments AS s
    ON b.customer_id = s.customer_id
    AND s.shipped_date < b.week_start + INTERVAL '7 days'
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY b.customer_id, b.week_start;
